name: Ritarungo
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_quote: On occasion I thought I had heard a noninitial long vowel, or at least an unexpected noninitial stress, but in the final pronunciation checks (mostly with the informant Goliath) I heard no consistent examples of noninitial length or irregular stress. (As these comments suggest, stress is normally on word-initial syllables.)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding fixed-strict initial rests on Heath 1980:11, the only grammar of Ritharrngu, held in full and quoted verbatim at the stated page (confirmed on p. 21 = printed p. 11). Heath's wording is mildly hedged ('normally on word-initial syllables', after reporting he found no consistent noninitial stress in final checks) and the surrounding phonology (vowel length contrast only in initial syllables; rule P-1 shortens long vowels made noninitial by prefixing/compounding) supports word-initial stress with the word as domain. No competing or newer description exists in Glottolog's 32 refs, ANU repository, Crossref or ELAR. The record's grade field is blank although the quote is verbatim-primary and verified; only action is to set the strength of the evidence accordingly. no reclassification indicated.
